hot_tub.shock_location: Extra shock on top of the fridge

mode_setup.must_do_first: Set the tub to ST (Standard) mode or it will not maintain temperature
mode_setup.why: In EC (Economy) mode the heater only runs during filter cycles, your water cools between them. ST keeps it at your set temp 24/7.
steps: Tap the Warm or Temp button to wake up the display
Press Mode (or hold Warm for 3 sec if no Mode button)
Display cycles through ST → EC → SL, stop when it shows ST
Then press Warm/Cool to set 102°F
mode_setup.video_tutorial_title: How to set ST vs EC mode (2 min)

quick_start: Confirm the display shows ST (see mode setup above)
Open jet valves before running jets
Use Warm/Cool button to set temp (100-102°F)
Add one shock after each use
rules: No food, drinks, or glass in the tub
Keep water above the filter line, drops below = heater shuts off
hot_tub.water_care: Shock every 2–3 days for light use, or after each heavy / long soak. No food, drinks, glass, or smoking in the water.
hot_tub.safety_kill_switch: The hot tub has a safety kill switch inside the water filter system. If the water level drops below the filter, the heating element stops working until you refill.
hot_tub.water_displacement: Be mindful of water displacement when entering and exiting the tub. Avoid causing the water level to drop below the filter line.
hot_tub.replenishing_water: Top up the tub with the garden hose any time the level looks low. The heating element only operates when water sits above the filter.

heating_instructions.control_panel: Marquis Spas come with a digital control panel that manages temperature, jet flow, and lighting. Comfortable soak temp is 100–102°F.
heating_instructions.jets_button: Tap the 'Jets' button once to turn the 2-speed pump on or to shift between low and high speeds. Low speed auto-shuts off after 2 hours, high speed after 15 minutes.
heating_instructions.warm_cool_button: Press 'Warm' or 'Cool' once and the set temperature flashes. Keep tapping to raise or lower it. Wait a few seconds for the flashing to stop and the new set point locks in.
heating_instructions.lights_and_features: If the spa has lighting or audio, the controls live on the same panel. Tap each one to experiment with settings.

casual_dinner.name: Saigon Bowl
casual_dinner.reason: Widely considered the best pho in Thornton. Twenty years of Vietnamese cooking behind every bowl.

parks.name: Trail Winds Park
parks.reason: 111 acres of natural beauty in Thornton, well-maintained trails, lush greenery, and expansive open spaces. Soccer and football courts plus bike paths make it good for active days. Expect to spot birds, rabbits, squirrels, and occasionally deer.

parks.name: Pecos Park
parks.reason: A peaceful 9.2-acre Thornton retreat with scenic trails and a calming atmosphere. Paths suit both leisurely strolls and faster runs. Wildlife sightings include rabbits, birds, the occasional deer, and foxes in the early morning or evening.

parks.name: Grange Creek Park
parks.reason: 16 acres of lush greenery and creekside views in Thornton. Trails and pathways for walking, running, and hiking. Year-round access. You might encounter deer, rabbits, various birds, and occasionally coyotes, keep your distance.

parks.name: Cherry Park
parks.reason: 24.2 acres of scenic trails and lush greenery, perfect for walking, running, and hiking with the dog. Easy parking, leisure playground, plus basketball and baseball courts. Birds, squirrels, rabbits, and occasional deer call this park home.

parks.name: Northstar Park
parks.reason: A walking and running haven in Thornton with a well-maintained baseball court for sprint drills. Plenty of parking and shelters for breaks. Birds, squirrels, rabbits, and possibly deer.

parks.name: Carstens Park
parks.reason: A peaceful 37-acre escape in Westminster. Tennis, basketball, and baseball courts plus well-maintained trails through lush greenery. Suitable for all fitness levels and year-round.

parks.name: Liberty Hills Park
parks.reason: A peaceful 2.8-acre Thornton retreat with vibrant flora and scenic trails. Welcoming year-round for leisurely strolls or invigorating runs. Birds, squirrels, rabbits, and occasionally deer.

adventure_day.name: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre
adventure_day.reason: A picture-perfect setting with flawless all-natural acoustics 70 million years in the making. Beyond the blockbuster summer concerts (the Beatles to U2 have played here), it's open year-round, visit the Red Rocks Performers Hall of Fame or hike the 1.4-mile Trading Post Loop Trail through the rock formations and meadows.

adventure_day.name: Lookout Mountain
adventure_day.address: Lookout Mountain Park, 1.7 miles west of downtown Golden
adventure_day.reason: A 7,377-foot foothill of the Rockies with sweeping views of downtown Denver, only 12 miles to the east. Earliest inhabitants were the Ute tribe, who used it as a literal lookout. Today you can hike, mountain bike, or cycle up the steep road for one of the best workouts and views on the Front Range.

adventure_day.name: Estes Park & Rocky Mountain National Park
adventure_day.reason: The classic Colorado day. Estes is the base for Rocky Mountain National Park, elk, mouse, bears, alpine lakes, and miles of trails. Trail Ridge Road winds past craggy peaks, forests, and tundra. While you're there, stop by The Stanley Hotel and check out the story behind The Shining.

adventure_day.name: Dinosaur Ridge
adventure_day.reason: A famous natural landmark along the Front Range with Jurassic dinosaur bones, Stegosaurus and Apatosaurus discovered here in 1877, plus Cretaceous footprints. Self-guided with a guidebook, or arrange a guided tour with Friends of Dinosaur Ridge.

adventure_day.name: Buffalo Bill Museum & Grave
adventure_day.reason: One of the most famous cowboys to ever ride the range, William F. "Buffalo Bill" Cody was buried atop Lookout Mountain at his own request. The museum (opened in 1921) has exhibits on his life, the Wild West shows, Indian artifacts including Sitting Bull's bows and arrows, Western art, and firearms.

adventure_day.name: American Mountaineering Museum
adventure_day.reason: A must-stop on your way to the mountains. From 14ers to Everest, the museum lets you experience mountaineering through interactive exhibits, cross a crevasse, pick your route up Everest, follow famous climbers' footsteps.

adventure_day.name: Boulder / Flatirons
adventure_day.reason: College town energy meets iconic rock formations. Pearl Street Mall, the University of Colorado campus, and easy hiking at Chautauqua. A solid half-day trip.

troubleshooting.issue: The hot tub isn't heating up
troubleshooting.intro: Nine times out of ten this is a low-water issue. The heater shuts itself off if the water drops below the filter line, a safety feature, not a malfunction.
steps: Lift the cover and check the water level. It should be above the top of the filter housing on the side of the tub.
If it's low, top it up with the garden hose at the back of the house. Aim for 2–3 inches above the filter line.
Make sure the display reads ST (Standard) mode. If you see EC, hold the Warm button for 3 seconds until ST appears.
Give it 15 minutes to recover. The temperature climbs about 2°F per hour.
Still not heating after an hour? Text us and we'll come take a look.

troubleshooting.issue: The hot tub jets won't turn on
troubleshooting.intro: Almost always a closed valve. The jets share air with the valves around the rim of the tub.
steps: Look around the rim of the tub for the silver dial valves (there are usually four).
Turn each one fully counter-clockwise until it stops. That opens the airflow.
Press the Jets button on the control panel once. The pump should kick on.
Press it a second time to switch to high speed. Press again to turn off.
If the pump still doesn't engage, text us, it may need a quick reset on our end.

troubleshooting.issue: The golf simulator isn't reading my shots
troubleshooting.intro: The SkyTrak unit uses a laser to track the ball, so it's all about how the ball faces the monitor.
steps: Tee up the ball with the label facing the screen, not the floor or the ceiling.
Make sure the SkyTrak unit is positioned exactly where the tape mark shows on the mat.
If a shot misreads, just take a mulligan. The system can occasionally miss a fast strike.
Confirm the green light on the SkyTrak is solid, not blinking. Blinking means it lost WiFi.
If it's blinking, open the SkyTrak app on the iPad and tap Reconnect.

troubleshooting.issue: The Wi-Fi feels slow or won't connect
troubleshooting.intro: Usually one device is hogging the bandwidth, or the network just needs a beat.
steps: Forget the network on your phone, then reconnect with the password from the cover of this book.
If multiple devices are streaming 4K, pause one of them and see if speeds come back.
Try the network named Kushkations.com (the 5 GHz band) if you're close to the router.
If everyone is offline, send us a text and we'll reboot the router remotely.

troubleshooting.issue: A TV is stuck on 'No Signal'
troubleshooting.intro: The TV input got bumped to the wrong HDMI port. Easy fix from the couch.
steps: Grab the TV remote (the small black one), not the Roku remote.
Press the Input or Source button.
Cycle through the inputs until you see HDMI 1, that's where the Roku lives.
Picture should come right back. Hand the Roku remote to whoever's choosing the show.
